tasks.short: Field manager and employee questions, read contracts and the CAO, and help sort out workplace problems.

today.trigger: A manager or employee mails, calls or messages on Teams about a contract, schedule, conflict or working conditions issue.
steps: Read the question and work out who and which site it concerns
Look up the contract, hours and history in AFAS Profit and the relevant CAO article
Call or meet the manager and/or employee to hear both sides
Agree an approach and write it up by mail
Note the outcome in the AFAS dossier or own Excel log
drudgery: Finding the right CAO clause and contract version each time
Rewriting the same explanation for different managers
Keeping a separate case log by hand
today.time_sinks: Lookup across AFAS, two CAOs and SharePoint before the real conversation, and chasing follow-up by mail across three sites.

lenses.faster: A case assistant pulls the employee's contract data, the matching CAO clause and earlier notes into one summary and drafts the follow-up mail; the lookup and write-up shrink, the conversations stay the same length.
lenses.autonomous: A new mail or Teams message tagged as a case opens a case record with a summary and sources; nothing reaches the employee or manager until the HRBP sends it.
lenses.ambitious: Shift leaders in warehouses and transport, who today rarely reach an HRBP, get same-day answers on contract and roster questions; demand would grow as it gets cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses hunting for the right CAO version or retyping case notes; HRBPs want more time on the floor sorting out real conflicts.
lenses.options: For a conflict, two or three drafted approaches (informal talk, mediation, formal route) with their CAO and dossier consequences help the HRBP and manager choose the route.
lenses.altitude: The week moves from answering lookups to running a case queue with fewer, harder cases; the HRBP decides which cases go formal and becomes more expert in conflict and labour law.
reach: Contract-change paperwork of the HR Administrator (needs AFAS mutation rules)
First-line CAO questions now sent to the Payroll Specialist (needs CAO pay-scale knowledge)

tasks.human_edge: Hearing both sides, reading tension in a team, and judging what is fair under the CAO and with the works council in mind stays with the HRBP.
tasks.pattern_why: Each case differs and the outcome rests on trust and judgment; AI only prepares facts and drafts for the HRBP who leads.

in_practice.trigger: Mail or Teams message to the HRBP mailbox flagged as a case.
steps: Assistant summarises the question and identifies employee, site and contract type
Pulls contract, hours and absence data from AFAS and the relevant CAO clause from SharePoint
Drafts a reply or talking points with sources
HRBP talks to the people involved and edits the draft
Outcome is logged to the case record
in_practice.human_gate: HRBP reviews every draft and decides the approach before anything is sent.
data_needed: Both CAO texts and house policies
in_practice.logs_to: Case list in SharePoint with source links, retained per AVG retention rules.

evidence.claim: IBM's AI front door handles routine questions and HRBPs act as the first human level for escalated complex cases.
Danish HR professionals using chatbots saved about 3% of hours on average.
An assistant processing personnel data needs works council consent under WOR art. 27.

risks: Wrong CAO version or outdated contract cited in a draft
Employees sense AI-written replies and trust drops
IT and AVG sign-off may limit AFAS data access to the assistant
research_questions: How many HRBP hours per week go to lookup versus conversation, measured over two weeks?
Can the AFAS Profit API expose contract data to Copilot within IT's data rules?
Will the works council consent to an assistant reading case notes?

tasks.short: Explain HR policies, CAO rules and laws like poortwachter and leave to managers and staff.

today.trigger: A question by mail, phone, Teams or at the site about leave, overtime, sickness rules, pay or a CAO article.
steps: Find the right policy, CAO article or legal rule
Check whether the person's contract changes the answer
Write or tell the answer in plain Dutch (or English for flex workers)
Answer follow-up questions
drudgery: Answering the same leave and overtime questions every week
Translating policy text into plain language again and again
today.time_sinks: Repeat questions that each need a lookup, especially at season peaks when flex workers arrive.

lenses.faster: A Teams bot answers general policy and CAO questions from owned SharePoint content with source links; the HRBP handles only escalations and checks a weekly sample.
lenses.autonomous: Any question to the bot is answered directly if it is general policy; questions about a personal case, sickness or dismissal go straight to the HRBP queue with a summary.
lenses.ambitious: Flex workers and night shifts, who today get no HR answer outside office hours, are served for the first time in Dutch, English and Polish; demand would clearly grow.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses the hundredth holiday-hours question; HRBPs want more time on the cases where the rule is unclear.
lenses.options: Little; a policy answer is right or wrong, so drafts matter only when a rule is ambiguous and the HRBP needs to pick an interpretation.
lenses.altitude: The HRBP owns the answer set: decides which topics the bot may answer, reviews wrong answers weekly, and rewrites unclear policy; the role becomes more expert in policy design.
reach: Policy upkeep on SharePoint now done by HR Administrators (needs content governance)
Absence-rule questions handled by the absence coordinator (needs poortwachter detail)

tasks.human_edge: Deciding how an unclear rule applies to a specific person, and noticing when a question hides a bigger problem, stays with the HRBP.
tasks.pattern_why: A fixed flow: retrieve from owned policy content, one model call to answer with sources, rules route personal cases to a person.

in_practice.trigger: Employee or manager asks the HR bot in Teams or the intranet.
steps: Bot states it is an AI assistant
Retrieves matching policy and CAO passages from SharePoint
Answers in the user's language with links to the source
Routes personal, sickness, dismissal or complaint questions to the HRBP queue
HRBP reviews flagged and sampled answers weekly
in_practice.human_gate: Escalated questions are answered by the HRBP; the HRBP approves any new topic before the bot may answer it.
systems: Copilot Studio or similar Teams bot
data_needed: Current CAO texts and house policies
in_practice.logs_to: Question and answer log with sources, kept for review and complaint handling.

evidence.claim: Coca-Cola Andina's HR agent serves 1,200 of 3,600 staff monthly with CSAT 4.1 and raises tickets for what it cannot answer.
IBM's Ask HR handles over 11 million interactions a year with self-reported 40% savings.
Employee-facing chatbots must disclose they are AI.

risks: Wrong answer on sickness or pay rules creates a legal or CAO dispute
Outdated SharePoint policies get served as truth
Flex workers' questions may concern agency terms the bot does not know
research_questions: What share of current questions is general policy versus personal case, from a month of HRBP mail?
Are SharePoint policies current enough to serve directly, or is a cleanup needed first?
Does the works council see the bot as needing consent under art. 27?
Would flex worker agencies allow the bot to answer about their terms?

tasks.short: Help managers place the right people in the right teams and roles across sites and shifts.

today.trigger: A reorganisation, peak season, a vacancy, or a manager asking to move staff between teams or sites.
steps: Collect who is available, their contract hours and site
Check certificates (forklift, VCA, food safety) in Studytube
Discuss fit and preferences with managers
Propose placements and agree with managers and employees
Have the HR Administrator process changes in AFAS
drudgery: Merging AFAS and Studytube exports in Excel
Checking which certificates expire before the move
today.time_sinks: Building the people-and-certificate overview by hand before any discussion.

lenses.faster: A standing qualification matrix joins AFAS contracts with Studytube certificates per site and shift, so the overview is ready and the HRBP spends time on the placement talks.
lenses.autonomous: A nightly job refreshes the matrix and flags gaps (no certified forklift driver on a Venlo night shift); people are placed only by managers and the HRBP.
lenses.ambitious: Placement decisions for flex workers converting to permanent contracts become a monthly review per site instead of an ad-hoc call; demand would grow modestly.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses the Excel merge; the HRBP wants more time talking with people about where they fit.
lenses.options: Two or three placement scenarios per peak (move staff from Tilburg, hire flex, cross-train) show cost and certificate gaps and change the choice.
lenses.altitude: The HRBP decides placement rules with operations managers and becomes a workforce planner per site, a more expert role.
reach: Certificate-expiry tracking from the L&D Specialist (needs Studytube reporting)
Headcount scenarios with the FP&A Analyst (needs basic cost modelling)

tasks.human_edge: Knowing who works well together, personal circumstances and what a move means for someone stays human; scoring people on traits would also become high-risk AI.
tasks.pattern_why: Matching contracts, sites and certificates follows written rules; a query and dashboard do it without a model.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly refresh, plus a manager's request for a move or peak plan.
steps: Join AFAS contract and site data with Studytube certificates
Show matrix and gaps per site and shift in Power BI
HRBP builds placement scenarios with the manager
Agreed moves go to the HR Administrator for AFAS
in_practice.human_gate: Manager and HRBP decide every placement; the employee is consulted.
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI refresh log and placement decisions in AFAS.

evidence.claim: Microsoft's Workforce Insights agent shows managers team structure and staffing without asking HR.
AI that allocates tasks based on behaviour or traits is high-risk from 2 December 2027.

risks: Studytube certificate data incomplete, so the matrix misleads
Scope creep into ranking people, which triggers high-risk rules and works council consent
research_questions: How complete and current are Studytube certificate records per site?
How many placement decisions per month would use the matrix?
Can Studytube and AFAS be joined on a shared employee number?

tasks.short: Advise managers on recruitment and retention plans, like keeping warehouse staff past 90 days.

today.trigger: High turnover at a site, hard-to-fill vacancies, peak season planning, or a manager's request.
steps: Pull vacancy, hire and exit figures from Recruitee, AFAS and Power BI
Talk with recruiters and managers about causes
Draft a proposal (referral bonus, onboarding change, flex-to-permanent route)
Present to management and agree actions
drudgery: Reconciling hire and exit numbers across systems
today.time_sinks: Assembling the numbers and reading exit-interview notes before forming a view.

lenses.faster: An assistant drafts the analysis from Power BI retention data and summarises exit reasons, and drafts the proposal deck; the HRBP checks and adds context.
lenses.autonomous: When 90-day retention at a site drops below an agreed threshold in Power BI, a summary with likely causes is prepared for the HRBP.
lenses.ambitious: Retention advice for each site and shift monthly instead of once a year, tied to the North Star; managers would ask for it more if cheap.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses reconciling exports; HRBPs want more time on designing and testing interventions with managers.
lenses.options: Drafting three interventions with cost and expected effect on 90-day retention (onboarding buddy, shift choice, flex conversion) changes what management picks.
lenses.altitude: The HRBP runs small experiments per site and decides which programme to scale; the job becomes more analytical and expert.
reach: Recruitment-source analysis now done by the Recruiter (needs Recruitee reporting)
Retention dashboards from the People Analytics Analyst (needs Power BI basics)

tasks.human_edge: Knowing the local labour market, site culture and what managers will actually carry out stays with the HRBP.
tasks.pattern_why: Advice is a judgment shaped with managers; AI speeds the analysis and drafting.

in_practice.trigger: Retention or time-to-hire signal in Power BI or a manager request.
steps: Pull retention and hiring figures per site
Summarise exit reasons from AFAS and interview notes
Draft scenarios and a short deck
HRBP reviews with recruiters and presents
in_practice.human_gate: HRBP owns the advice and presents it; management decides.
data_needed: Hires and exits by site and source
Cost per hire and agency rates

evidence.claim: General model knowledge: LLMs can summarise free-text exit reasons and draft scenario decks from tabular data.

risks: Exit notes contain personal data; AVG limits on processing
Small numbers per site make causes look clearer than they are
research_questions: Are exit reasons recorded consistently in AFAS?
Has any retention intervention at Noordhaven been measured against 90-day retention?
Do managers act on site-level advice more than on annual reports?

tasks.short: Coach and train managers on interviewing, appraisals, difficult conversations and documenting performance issues.

today.trigger: A new manager, the appraisal cycle, or a performance issue a manager raises.
steps: Prepare or adapt training material and checklists
Run sessions or one-to-one coaching
Help managers prepare a difficult conversation
Review the manager's written documentation of a performance issue
drudgery: Rewriting the same guidance for each manager
today.time_sinks: One-to-one preparation for each difficult conversation and fixing documentation after the fact.

lenses.faster: A copilot drafts conversation plans and checks a manager's performance notes against a checklist (facts, dates, agreed actions) before the HRBP looks.
lenses.autonomous: When a manager logs a performance concern, they get a preparation guide and a text role-play to practise; the HRBP joins only for formal cases.
lenses.ambitious: Coaching for every team and shift leader on all three sites, including night shifts, for the first time; demand would grow as it gets cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses fixing vague notes; HRBPs want more of the live coaching itself.
lenses.options: Two or three openings for a hard conversation let the manager pick a tone that fits the person.
lenses.altitude: The HRBP designs the manager programme and coaches on the hardest cases; more expert as a coach.
reach: Manager training modules of the L&D Specialist (needs Studytube course building)

tasks.human_edge: Reading a manager's confidence, and judging when a case needs the HRBP in the room, stays human.
tasks.pattern_why: The manager and HRBP lead; AI drafts, checks and offers practice.

in_practice.trigger: Manager requests help or appraisal cycle starts.
steps: Manager opens the coaching assistant in Teams
Gets a conversation plan and text role-play
Assistant checks documentation for missing facts
HRBP reviews formal cases
in_practice.human_gate: HRBP reviews any documentation that may feed a formal procedure.
in_practice.logs_to: Coaching use statistics only; no content stored per employee without consent.

evidence.claim: IBM nudges managers and pilots role-play for difficult conversations, without outcome data.
Workday HRBP-built check-in agent raised share of 'Good' feedback by 16 points vs 7 for non-users.
Employees may notice AI-drafted feedback and close off.

risks: Emotion inference from voice in role-play is banned at work (Art. 5)
Tool that evaluates performance becomes high-risk from December 2027
research_questions: Do managers' performance files improve in quality after using the checklist?
Will shift leaders use a Teams tool on their phones?
Does the works council see a documentation checker as performance monitoring?

tasks.short: Set up ways to measure staff satisfaction and the complaint and grievance procedures.

today.trigger: Yearly survey planning, a works council request, or a pattern of complaints.
steps: Design or update the survey and complaint procedure
Agree with the works council
Run the survey or pulse
Set up follow-up per site
today.time_sinks: Back-and-forth on question design and the works council approval process.

lenses.faster: AI drafts survey questions, translations and procedure texts from benchmarks; the HRBP edits and takes them to the works council.
lenses.autonomous: Little; designing methods is rare and needs consent, so it stays HRBP-led.
lenses.ambitious: Short pulse surveys in several languages for flex workers and night shifts, heard for the first time; demand would grow if cheap.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses formatting forms; HRBPs want more time acting on results with managers.
lenses.options: Comparing designs (annual survey vs monthly pulse vs anonymous complaint line) changes what the works council approves.
lenses.altitude: The HRBP decides the listening method with the works council and becomes more expert in measurement and employee voice.
reach: Survey analysis from the People Analytics Analyst (needs basic statistics)

tasks.human_edge: Building trust with the works council and employees that their voice is safe stays human.
tasks.pattern_why: Design work negotiated with the works council; AI only drafts.

in_practice.trigger: Survey cycle or works council request.
steps: Draft question set and translations
HRBP edits and agrees with the works council
Configure in Forms
Set up complaint routing
in_practice.human_gate: Works council consent and HRBP approval before launch.
in_practice.logs_to: Design decisions and works council agreement on SharePoint.

evidence.claim: Works council consent is needed for systems that observe behaviour or performance (WOR art. 27).
People affected by an AI outcome must always be able to complain.

risks: Text sentiment over Teams chat is monitoring and needs consent
research_questions: Would flex workers answer a pulse survey in their own language?
What response rate did the last survey reach per site?
Will the works council approve monthly pulses?

tasks.short: Turn satisfaction survey and complaint data into reports and presentations for management.

today.trigger: Survey closes or quarterly management meeting.
steps: Export results to Excel
Calculate scores per site and team
Read and group open comments
Build PowerPoint slides
Present to management and works council
drudgery: Coding hundreds of open comments by hand

lenses.faster: Scores flow into a Power BI dashboard and one model step groups open comments into themes with example quotes; the HRBP checks the themes and writes the key message.
lenses.autonomous: When a survey closes, the dashboard updates and a draft report is ready; it goes out only after the HRBP signs off.
lenses.ambitious: Each site and shift manager gets their own report every quarter, not one company report a year; demand would grow.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses coding comments; HRBPs want more time discussing actions with managers.
lenses.options: Little; the report describes, but different framings for management and works council may matter.
lenses.altitude: The HRBP spends time on follow-up actions rather than slides; decides which themes go to management.
reach: Dashboard upkeep from the People Analytics Analyst (needs Power BI skills)

tasks.human_edge: Choosing what the data means for the business and how to present sensitive results stays with the HRBP.
tasks.pattern_why: A fixed reporting flow with one model call to theme open comments; the rest is a dashboard.

steps: Load scores into Power BI
Model step themes comments with quotes, small groups suppressed
Draft report generated
HRBP reviews and adds the message
in_practice.human_gate: HRBP approves each report before it is shared.

evidence.claim: Digest recommends dashboards plus an LLM step over comments for satisfaction reports.

risks: Quotes reveal identity in small teams
research_questions: Do model-generated themes match an HRBP's manual coding on last year's survey?
What minimum group size keeps anonymity?

role.altitude: The HRBP stops being the first stop for policy questions and becomes the second line for complex cases, owning the answer set, manager coaching programme and site-level retention experiments tied to 90-day retention.
reach: General policy questions now handled by HR Administrators
Retention and survey dashboards from the People Analytics Analyst
Manager training modules from the L&D Specialist
role.ceiling_note: Conversations, conflicts, dismissals and works council relations stay human; savings concentrate in policy explanation and reporting, roughly 25-30% of role hours overall, limited by AFAS data access, works council consent and EU AI Act high-risk rules from December 2027.
skills_to_grow: Writing and maintaining bot content and escalation rules
Power BI and basic people analytics
Works council and AI Act compliance
role.ambitious_version: Every shift leader and flex worker on all three sites gets same-day HR answers and coaching in their own language, while HRBPs run monthly site-level experiments on 90-day retention.
